description: Provides safety-focused guidance for pushing a selected workspace project to GitHub without accidentally publishing unrelated or sensitive files.
useCase: Developers and agent operators use this skill when publishing workspace files to GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket from a shared or parent Git repository. It helps verify repository boundaries, stage only intended files, configure basic ignore rules, and use a GitHub Contents API fallback when ordinary git push repeatedly times out.

risks.risk: Workspace files could be published with secrets, unrelated projects, or large generated folders if the wrong directory or staged file list is used.
risks.mitigation: Confirm the exact target directory, repository visibility, and explicit staged file list before pushing; inspect git status for secrets and unrelated files.

risks.risk: A project inside a parent Git repository could pollute the parent history or expose files outside the intended project.
risks.mitigation: Compare the Git top-level directory with the target directory and initialize an isolated repository when the target is nested inside a parent repository.

output.format: Markdown guidance with shell command examples and checklists
